questions.q: $A$ is $3 \times 4$ and $B$ is $4 \times 2$. What is the shape of $C = A B$?
questions.explain: $A_{m \times n} B_{n \times p} = C_{m \times p}$: the inner 4s match and cancel, leaving $3 \times 2$.

questions.q: Which pair of shapes **cannot** be multiplied as $A B$?
questions.explain: The inner dimensions must match: a row of $A$ has 3 numbers but a column of $B$ has only 2, so they cannot be paired up for a dot product.
$C[1,2]$ = row 1 of $A$ · column 2 of $B$ $= 1 \cdot 1 + 2 \cdot (-1) = -1$. Using column 1 instead gives 2.

questions.q: For $A$ of shape $(m, n)$ and $B$ of shape $(n, p)$, how many multiply-then-add terms go into one output cell $C[i, j]$?
questions.explain: $C[i, j] = \sum_k A[i, k]\,B[k, j]$ runs over the shared inner index $k = 1, \dots, n$.
